summary: Makes engine registration and tenancy choices understandable by pairing clearer labels with visible explanations and required-field guidance.
userImpact: The Add Engine and Edit Engine forms identify required, optional, and conditionally required settings before submission.
Connection, tenancy, runtime-access, deployment, and authentication choices use plain-language labels with an explanation of the selected behavior.
Topology transitions and tenant-mapping strategies explain what each option does and distinguish tenant mappings from native authorization group mappings.
Editing an OAuth 2.0 engine no longer requires replacing an already stored client secret.
documentation: The in-product Engine form and tenancy panel now provide the user-facing guidance; no operator procedure or configuration contract changes.
rollback: Redeploy the previous frontend-host package or application image; engine configuration data is unchanged.
validation: Focused frontend tests cover required-field indicators, selected-option explanations, conditional requirements, and terminology distinctions.
Browser UI evidence covers the Add Engine form, tenant-ownership controls, explained dropdowns, responsive reflow, and accessible labels.
